payload.title: Aperture, exposure and photographic blur

model.title: Aperture, exposure and photographic blur
model.description: Unqualified teaching proposal for human review: ideal thin-lens exposure, depth of field and transverse motion blur; schematic photograph comparisons only.
assumptions: Adjustable illustrative defaults and bounds: aperture_number default 8, range 2–16; shutter_duration default 0.008 s, range 0.001–0.125 s; elapsed_time default 0 s, range 0–10 s.
Lighting is uniform and fixed; illustrative ISO is fixed at 100. Received exposure is proportional to duration/f-number², relative to f/8 at 0.008 s.
Fixed illustrative optics: focal length 0.05 m, focus distance 3 m, acceptable image-plane defocus diameter 0.00003 m. Foreground and background lie at 2 m and 9 m.
Paraxial thin-lens depth boundaries are s/[1±N*c*(s-f)/f²], with plus for near and minus for far. All denominators remain positive.
Defocus diameter at distance z is (f/N)*f*abs(z-s)/[z*(s-f)]. Fixed dimensionless coefficients evaluate this expression at the foreground and background planes. Focused-plane defocus is zero.
The focused subject moves transversely at a fixed illustrative 1 m/s, remaining at 3 m depth. Image speed magnitude is subject speed times f/(s-f).
Coordinates: positive scene depth runs from lens toward objects; subject motion is positive x. Sensor distance is measured behind the lens. Image motion reverses transverse direction.
An ideal global shutter opens at elapsed_time=0 and closes at shutter_duration. Subject position starts at x=0; no blade or curtain trajectory is modeled.

Time experiment: elapsed_time; step_seconds 0.001; playback_speed 0.1; reset_on_change [aperture_number, shutter_duration]; end_time_id null. Parameter changes restart time atomically; pause remains respected.
Equal-exposure examples: f/4 at 0.002 s, f/8 at 0.008 s, f/16 at 0.032 s. These preserve received exposure, not defocus or motion blur.
All outputs are bounded across the stated input ranges. Near distance is approximately 1.915–2.802 m; far distance approximately 3.229–6.919 m. No denominator vanishes.
limitations: Representative ideal paraxial optics, not a product-specific or calibrated camera model.
Relative received light is not rendered brightness. Saturation, clipping, noise, absolute photon counts and image processing are not predicted.
The acceptable-defocus criterion is an illustrative viewing assumption, not a universal sharpness threshold.
Defocus and motion are separate measurements, not a synthesized combined point-spread function or photorealistic photograph.
Diffraction, aberrations, camera shake, rolling shutter, autofocus, exposure automation and mechanical shutter dynamics are excluded.
Final exposure and blur readouts describe the complete selected exposure; accumulated readouts describe elapsed open time. Subject motion continues after closure.

limits: Illustrative apparatus, not a measured camera or manufacturer design.

Object distances and transverse travel use one scene unit per metre on every axis. The lens origin is (0,2,0); positive depth is +Z and subject movement is +X. Camera housing and internal inspection features are enlarged teaching representations, not a distance scale; sensor_distance remains the accepted SI calculation.
Aperture f-number defaults to 8 with range 2–16; shutter duration defaults to 0.008 s with range 0.001–0.125 s; elapsed time spans 0–10 s.
Lighting and ISO 100 remain fixed. Focal length is 0.05 m, focus distance 3 m, criterion diameter 0.00003 m, and subject speed 1 m/s. Foreground and background distances are 2 m and 9 m.
Relative received exposure is not rendered image brightness. Clipping, saturation, noise, photon counts and image processing are not predicted.

Paraxial thin-lens defocus uses an illustrative viewing criterion, not a universal sharpness threshold. Defocus and motion remain separate measurements, not a combined point-spread function or photorealistic photograph.

Diffraction, aberrations, camera shake, rolling shutter, autofocus, exposure automation and mechanical shutter trajectories are excluded. The highlighted aperture is an ideal opening indicator, not simulated iris blades.

The shutter indicator reports the ideal global open flag; no curtain motion is implied. Final readouts describe the selected complete exposure; accumulated readouts stop accumulating at closure while the subject keeps moving throughout the clock range.

parts.label: Optical teaching bench
parts.explanation: The bench supports the camera and distance targets.

parts.label: Camera body
parts.explanation: The hollow body holds the lens and image plane. Open its shell to see inside.

parts.label: Rear cover
parts.explanation: This cover closes the back of the camera.

parts.label: Lens barrel
parts.explanation: The hollow barrel holds the optical parts in line.

parts.label: Ideal lens
parts.explanation: The lens represents the thin lens used in the calculations. Its drawn thickness is only for inspection.

parts.label: Lens retaining ring
parts.explanation: This open ring holds the lens edge without blocking its centre.

parts.label: Aperture surround
parts.explanation: This ring locates the aperture behind the lens. The highlighted centre shows the ideal opening.

parts.label: Clear aperture
parts.explanation: This highlighted circle shows the opening that admits light. A smaller f-number makes it wider.

parts.label: Image-plane holder
parts.explanation: This open frame holds the image plane behind the lens.

parts.label: Image plane
parts.explanation: The focused picture forms here. The displayed lens-to-image distance comes from the thin-lens calculation.

parts.label: Shutter timing indicator
parts.explanation: This indicator tells you whether the ideal shutter is open. It does not show moving shutter curtains.

parts.label: Foreground target · 2 m
parts.explanation: This nearby striped target can look out of focus. Its calculated defocus is compared with the chosen blur criterion.

parts.label: Focused moving target · 3 m
parts.explanation: This target moves sideways at 1 metre per second while staying at the focused distance. Its movement during the open shutter makes a trail.

parts.label: Background target · 9 m
parts.explanation: This distant striped target shows background defocus. It stays beyond the acceptable-defocus range for these settings.

parts.label: Photograph comparison display
parts.explanation: This display holds two simplified photographs for comparison. They are diagrams, not predictions of picture brightness.

parts.label: Reference photograph
parts.explanation: This panel represents the f/8, 0.008-second reference. Compare sharpness and trails separately from received light.

parts.label: Selected photograph
parts.explanation: This panel represents your selected settings. Equal received exposure need not mean equal sharpness or motion trails.

experiments.title: Follow the moving subject
experiments.prompt: Predict whether the subject stops when the shutter closes, then advance the clock to 0.02 s.
experiments.explanation: The focused target moves at the fixed illustrative 1 m/s. Accumulated received exposure stops increasing at shutter closure, but target motion continues. This readout measures light, not blur length.

experiments.title: Open the aperture
experiments.prompt: Keep shutter duration fixed. Predict the opening and received-light changes when you choose f/4.
experiments.explanation: The aperture indicator widens as f-number decreases. Its larger area increases relative received exposure at fixed duration, lighting and ISO; rendered brightness is not predicted.

experiments.title: Compare the foreground
experiments.prompt: Predict whether the foreground enters the acceptable-defocus range at f/16, then compare the near limit with 2 m.
experiments.explanation: A higher f-number narrows the opening and moves the near boundary toward the camera. Focus remains at 3 m. The viewing criterion is illustrative; the 9 m background remains outside the range.

experiments.title: Match light, not the whole photograph
experiments.prompt: Set f/4 and 0.002 s, then change only aperture to f/8. Predict whether changing duration to 0.008 s restores the original light ratio.
experiments.explanation: Compare after each change. These two combinations preserve duration divided by squared f-number. Their defocus and motion lengths differ in the accepted model; the available numeric readout confirms received exposure only, not photograph equivalence.

controls.help: A lower f-number widens the ideal opening, increases received light and increases defocus at fixed object distances.
Longer duration increases received light and moving-subject image travel; lighting, ISO and subject speed stay fixed.
Advance the moving target and accumulated exposure; light accumulation stops at closure while the target keeps moving.

time_experiment.explanation: The target starts at x=0 and moves at a fixed illustrative 1 m/s. Open time is min(elapsed time, shutter duration); exposure and image travel accumulate only during that interval. Parameter changes restart time atomically and respect pause. Subject motion continues after closure; no mechanical shutter trajectory is modeled.

coverage.explanation: The independent settings determine ideal opening area and duration/f-number² received exposure. Lighting and ISO remain fixed; brightness and clipping are excluded.

Aperture changes the displayed near acceptable-defocus boundary with focal length, focus distance and viewing criterion fixed. Compare it with the 2 m foreground. Other accepted defocus quantities are not numeric readouts in this assembly.

Clock-driven subject travel and shutter closure illustrate the recording interval. The accepted model computes image travel during that interval, but this assembly exposes accumulated light rather than a numeric blur readout. Camera shake is excluded.

The declared equal-exposure pairs preserve the displayed light ratio while aperture changes the displayed near boundary. The model also changes motion blur, but this assembly lacks a numeric blur readout. Comparison panels are schematic, not photorealistic.

outcomes: Compare how aperture and shutter duration affect exposure when lighting and ISO remain fixed.
Observe how aperture changes depth of field with focal length and focus distance held fixed.
Observe how shutter duration changes blur from a moving subject.
Compare aperture–shutter combinations that preserve exposure but change depth of field or motion blur.

generation_quality.scope: Recipe, label, connection and dependency checks only. Dependency paths do not prove numeric change. Overlap, recognizability, physical correctness and child usability require separate evaluation.

visual.scope: Eight fitted views; projected bounds, center-ray occlusion, conservative bounding-box overlaps and estimated two-line label capacity. These heuristics do not replace rendered-image or child usability review.

sampled_quality.scope: Defaults, five points per input plus presets, a midpoint context for apparently inactive controls, all-input endpoints, and lesson experiments. Finite geometry and observed changes only; no proof of scientific accuracy, recognizability or complete state-space coverage.
